title: A Story That Can't Be Shared

lines.en: Her expression stiffening, Anna Croft quietly drew a dagger behind her back.
“······Supreme King.”
Regardless, Yoo Joonghyuk strode forward.
“Birds of a feather, I see. Do you feel some kinship because you both know the future?”
“······You know about the future too, don't you?”
“What I experienced wasn't the future.”
Rumble!
“Those were all ‘things that had happened’. The past.”
Things that had happened.
The story I had read was one Yoo Joonghyuk had lived through in his own flesh.
Dying thousands of times.
As though responding to those years, the [Black Heavenly Demon Sword] in his hand howled fiercely.
Anna Croft glanced at me.
I said,
“Go. He came to see me.”
“I hope next time I can hear your goal from your own mouth.”
With those words, Anna Croft vanished into the portal.
Certainly, she had no reason to stay now. Helping me this far had more than repaid her debt.
Yoo Joonghyuk didn't stop her. Normally, he would have pursued her relentlessly and cut her throat, but he didn't.
“Yoo Joonghyuk.”
I called him. Yoo Joonghyuk didn't look at me. He merely gazed into the empty portal entrance.
I called him once more.
“Listen to me. You did call me your companion once, after all.”
Turning toward me, Yoo Joonghyuk slowly drew his sword.
“Once.”
I couldn't fathom the anger in that cold voice.
[Activating the exclusive skill, ‘Omniscient Reader's Viewpoint’!]
And so, once again, I step into the curse of omniscience (全知).
[Your understanding of this person is insufficient!]
But Yoo Joonghyuk's inner world wouldn't admit me.
As though the person before me wasn't the one I'd known until now.
“I know what you're going to say. About that book.”
“You looked into my life through that story, and made my life your entertainment. Is there anything else I need to know?”
I couldn't make excuses. It was true.
What I'd done was no different from what the constellations had done.
I knew. I knew that. But······.
But was that all there was to his sense of betrayal?
[Your understanding of this person gradually rises!]
Yoo Joonghyuk waited for me. Like a judge searching for a clue to a false accusation—a clue he had never managed to find.
But I didn't know what to say, or how.
His emotions, flowing in through ‘Omniscient Reader's Viewpoint’, were filling my mind with darkness.
The sentences I knew were being covered by sentences I didn't know.
The words I should have said, and the words I wanted to say, were buried and lost beneath those pitch-black waves of emotion.
Then Yoo Joonghyuk's sword moved.
Even then, it didn't feel real. That he would truly kill me. That he would kill me, leaving behind all the time we'd spent together.
[The ‘Fruit of Good and Evil’ influences your emotions!]
[The ‘Fourth Wall’ shakes violently!]
The moment I saw the sword tip come within inches of my face, resentment surged alongside guilt.
[The ‘Fruit of Good and Evil’ draws out your dark emotions!]
I had tried quite hard.
Since the scenarios began, I'd really put everything I had into living.
I'd done my best, in my own way, to put what I'd read into practice.
I had never meant to hurt Yoo Joonghyuk or my companions.
I had thought only of the scenarios. How could I reduce the harm? How could I reliably reach an intact ending?
That was all. That was all it had been.
How on earth had things come to this?
Claaaang!
Bright blue sparks flew with a sharp clash.
“What are you standing there staring for, idiot!”
Han Sooyoung was there.
It wasn't by chance that Han Sooyoung came to Middle Island 3.
While undertaking the Small Island scenario, she had dreamed.
A dream of a man in a white coat killed by a man in a black coat.
It was an old, meaningless dream, so as she dreamed it, Han Sooyoung muttered, ‘This dream again.’
A dream was only a dream, after all, and dreams didn't happen in reality.
Just as a novel couldn't become reality.
—My third-round self is rather dim. Still not getting it after seeing the same scene over and over······.
‘What?’
Startled, Han Sooyoung turned toward the voice.
A woman in a black coat stood there. A similar build to hers. A face she couldn't see, as though someone had deliberately erased it.
That face kept speaking.
—However I look at it, your round seems headed for ruin at this rate······.
Feeling an instinctive fear, Han Sooyoung stepped back a couple of paces. But this was her dream. No one could run away inside their own dream.
—You know, I really like wrecking other people's schemes.
The moment the figure in the dream reached out, information she couldn't understand flowed into Han Sooyoung's mind.
[The power of ‘Predictive Plagiarism’ awakens within you!]
Then Han Sooyoung woke. Information she couldn't understand drifted through her head, and her consciousness began piecing it together through deduction, all on its own.
Soon, the following sentence appeared in her mind.
—Yoo Joonghyuk will head to Middle Island 3.

She didn't know why that sentence had come to mind. Still, Han Sooyoung decided to try following it. She didn't know what this mysterious dream was or who the figure in it was, but she felt that she ‘had to’.
And Han Sooyoung reached this place.
“Move. I have no business with you.”
Yoo Joonghyuk, glaring at her with a terrifying look.
Kim Dokja, staring at her with a dazed expression.
Han Sooyoung slowly drew a breath.
She didn't know what the dream wanted to show her. But at this moment, she understood her role.
Wearing her usual insolent grin, she spoke.
“I knew you'd cause trouble someday. That ‘Yoo Joonghyuk’ wouldn't change so easily.”
“If you don't move······.”
“What, you'll kill me? What will that gain you? Will it compensate for all the time you've been deceived?”
Yoo Joonghyuk didn't answer. Instead, his sword tip vanished.
With a faint laugh, Han Sooyoung met his sword as it shot through the air.
“······Honestly, you and Kim Dokja are exactly alike when it comes to not listening.”
[The constellation, ‘Abyssal Black Flame Dragon’, roars!]
The power of [Black Flame] dwelling throughout her body collided with his sword tip.
With the power of the second generation behind them, Yoo Joonghyuk's sword strikes were heavy. Biting her lip until it bled, Han Sooyoung unleashed her power.
Yoo Joonghyuk was strong. But she hadn't spent her time doing nothing, either.
[The Story, ‘Disciple of the Legendary Swordmaster’, shines!]
A Story she had barely managed to obtain before coming here, with every ounce of effort she could muster.
A swordmaster's power surged through her entire body.
Bzzzzzt!
Perhaps not elsewhere, but here.
“When someone talks······.”
Through dark-blue sparks, [Black Flame] transformed into aura surged toward Yoo Joonghyuk.
“You! Should! Listen!”
Bundles of aura pouring out with each clipped beat of her words.
Yoo Joonghyuk's gaze wavered at the unexpectedly fierce resistance.
Han Sooyoung seized the opening and shouted.
“Kim Dokja just read a novel! A horribly boring, long novel!”
Watching Yoo Joonghyuk give ground little by little, she thought she could do it.
This wasn't a complicated conflict. A misunderstanding born of words people had put together.
So she believed it could be resolved with words.
“Talk! Open up and talk to each other! Like other people!”
The persistent [Black Flame] was spreading onto Yoo Joonghyuk's sword.
Coldly shaking it off, he said,
“You don't know.”
“I do.”
Han Sooyoung growled at the way his cold tone shut her out.
“What makes you so furious? That Kim Dokja approached you already knowing about you? You're the same. Just like him, you've known things ahead of everyone else and deceived other people.”
Perhaps those words lit the spark. Anger entered Yoo Joonghyuk's eyes, too.
Their swords clashed in midair again.
“Of course I know you were sincere. I know you did it to save those people, to reach a better world. ······What do you think Kim Dokja was doing?”
“What kind of person throws their own life away because a character is going to die!”
Seeing his sword hesitate, Han Sooyoung kept pouring out words.
“Have you forgotten what Kim Dokja has done until now? Are you going to deny everything you've built in the third round just because he read that boring novel?”
Yoo Joonghyuk's Status was shrinking back.
Almost there. Han Sooyoung could feel it.
One more sentence, and she could stop this unnecessary fight.
“Calm down and think.”
But at the last moment, she took a wrong step.
“You're not that kind of character.”
“······Character?”
Yoo Joonghyuk's expression was changing.
It wasn't a question.
She realized her mistake too late. She couldn't take back what she'd already said.
“You're the same, too.”
Immense waves of magic power began spreading between their crossed blades.
Han Sooyoung's sword cried out in pain. The waves of [Black Flame] were being overwhelmed.
[The Story, ‘Torch That Swallowed the Myth’, roars!]
The [Giant Story] Yoo Joonghyuk had built was running wild.
“I saw what your 1863rd-round self did.”
“The 1863rd round? What are you—”
At that moment, something occurred to Han Sooyoung.
—The worldline of Ways of Survival's 1863rd round. ······Oh, you were there too. Though I don't know which one is the main body.
Kim Dokja had certainly said that once.
‘Could it be?’
Information coming together in her head.
She existed in the 1863rd round, too.
And there, she was living through another round.
Then that figure in the dream······.
The moment Han Sooyoung reached her answer, a split-second opening appeared.
Yoo Joonghyuk's sword didn't miss it.
Why couldn't I move?
Why hadn't I fought alongside Han Sooyoung?
Watching her speak for me, why couldn't I raise my voice with hers?
“You······ aren't good at telling your own story.”
I gathered Han Sooyoung into my arms as she lay looking up at me.
Blood poured from her waist in surges. Blood so vivid and red it didn't feel real.
Bleeding, she spoke.
“Kim Dokja. I know the ending you want.”
A playful smile, as always.
As though wiping away the blood on my cheek, Han Sooyoung brushed it with her hand and murmured,
“You poor bastard······.”
Staunching her bleeding, I frantically took out medicinal ingredients.
Her internal injuries were too severe. A merciless wound.
Second-generation sword aura had completely destroyed her insides.
I could save her.
If I had just a little more time.
If I found a proper physician and got her treated.
······But could I?
Han Sooyoung's hand, resting against my cheek, fell limply.
I called Han Sooyoung's name. Over and over, then over and over again.
But Han Sooyoung didn't rise.
Instead, I heard Yoo Joonghyuk's voice.
“Stand up, Kim Dokja.”
A voice in which I could sense neither guilt nor agitation.
At that moment, something snapped inside me, too.
I slowly rose.
[Yoo Joonghyuk.]
Stories seethed in my head.
—Some Stories are so large they're difficult to read properly. If you don't keep your balance, they can sweep you away at any time.
Yoo Hoseong had said that.
I knew it well, too. The larger the Stories grew, the heavier my burden became.
That was why I had gathered companions. We built a history together, created Stories.
To reach a different ending from Yoo Joonghyuk's in the original novel, I had come this far.
And this was the result.
Should I keep reading a story like this?
[The Giant Story, ‘Demon Realm's Spring’, begins its story.]
I had imagined an end we would all reach together.
I had believed such a story was surely possible.
[The Giant Story, ‘Torch That Swallowed the Myth’, begins its story.]
But if that was impossible.
If all the time I'd put in until now had been utterly useless.
[Activating ‘Demon King Transformation’.]
The ending I dreamed of no longer meant anything.
[I will kill you, Yoo Joonghyuk.]
「“I will kill you, Yoo Joonghyuk.”」
Everyone in the library was watching that sentence.
「(······One wrong turn, and we might all die.)」
[The ‘Fourth Wall’ vibrates violently!]
The entire library was shaking. Neatly arranged books fell into disarray. Yet no librarian was putting them back.
「(How frustrating. Why won't they talk? They really don't have enough desire to become one.)」
「(What did our poor Sooyoung ever do······.)」
The squid poked its round eyes with its legs.
The sentences continue.
Whenever Yoo Joonghyuk's and Kim Dokja's swords collided, Nirvana's teeth chattered.
「(Hey, rookie. What do you think?)」
At those words, Yoo Sangah turned toward the librarians, catching books flying overhead one by one.
Her hands were full of Kim Dokja's memories. The books she had been reading until a moment ago.
「(Well, I have two thoughts.)」
「(First, Sooyoung-ssi isn't dead. I know her well. She's not someone who'd risk her life for something like this.)」
The weeping squid's eyes widened.
「(What? But you saw it too.)」
「(You still don't understand. The heroine drops her hand and loses consciousness right there. Then the male protagonist awakens! In every movie I've seen—)」
Whatever the squid and Simulation said, Yoo Sangah quietly continued.
「(Second, the two of them are talking.)」
Looking at the accumulating sentences, she said,
「(Though no one in the world would call that a ‘conversation’.)」
Story fragments spill from a split arm.
The Stories we had built.
[The Story, ‘Demon Realm's Spring’, pours out its story!]
[The Story, ‘Torch That Swallowed the Myth’, growls!]
Story collides with Story, like a dragon and tiger grappling.
Possessing the same ‘Giant Stories’ as me, Yoo Joonghyuk was answering with the same power.
[You hold the larger stake in this Story!]

Despite my larger stake, the shares of the Stories belonging to Yoo Joonghyuk wouldn't listen to me. Perhaps it was because of the years he had accumulated. He had continued his story more fiercely than anyone in the <Star Stream>.
Bzzzzzt!
Second-generation probability was restraining us.
But some things couldn't be restrained.
[The Story, ‘One Who Opposes the Extraordinary’, shouts!]
[The Story, ‘One Who Opposes the Extraordinary’, roars in fury!]
The same Stories, built from the same history, collided.
[The ‘island's owner’ is paying attention to you.]
[Many constellations watch your battle.]
[The constellation, ‘Demon-like Judge of Fire’, ······.]
The constellations' voices were growing distant.
[The exclusive skill, ‘Fourth Wall’, activates!]
We swing our swords, each prepared to kill the other.
My desperate sword swing grazes Yoo Joonghyuk's waist, and his sword immediately thrusts at my shoulder in retaliation.
His combat sense was superior. But my ‘Status’ was higher.
[The Giant Story, ‘Demon Realm's Spring’, protects you!]
The transcendent's keen edge, piercing that thick Status as it flies toward me. In his sword aura, I read his sincerity. How desperately he stands here.
He didn't ask, and I didn't answer.
We merely swung our swords, again and again.
And in our place, the Stories continued speaking.
[The Story, ‘Paradise of Despair’, lunges like a wild beast!]
Memories of Paradise.
[The Story, ‘One Who Hunted the King of Disasters’, roars!]
Traces of [Peace Land].
[The Story, ‘Liberator of the Industrial Complex’, grieves.]
The days of revolution.
「These were sentences found nowhere in ‘Ways of Survival’.」
The time we had lived wasn't the same as any page I'd read.
[Activating ‘Angel Transformation’!]
Wings bursting through my shoulders. My momentarily amplified Status flowed into [Unbreakable Faith].
With a tremendous roar, Yoo Joonghyuk was thrown into the air, unable to withstand the impact.
“Come at me properly, Yoo Joonghyuk. I'll do the same.”
His eyes changed. The shape of the Status rising around him began to twist. Status strong enough to distort space. The true power of a high-stage transcendent was being unleashed.
Wrapped in golden radiance, Yoo Joonghyuk vanished.
[Omniscient Reader's Viewpoint ‘Stage 2’ is active.]
His sword moved too quickly for my eyes to follow.
Clang-clang-clang!
One strike, then another. With every clash, my wrist grew heavier. Stories poured from my thigh, and Stories flowed from Yoo Joonghyuk's shoulder.
Naturally, I began to hear his voice, too.
[The ‘Fourth Wall’ activates with great force, as though resisting!]
Yoo Joonghyuk was beginning his story.
I imagine the sentence that will follow.
Surely he would blame me.
As Han Sooyoung said, that was the kind of person you were.
「Why did you choose to stay in that round?」
Memories of the 1863rd round flashed through my mind.
「“I won't return to the third round. I'll stay here and see the ending with the people of this place.”」
The choice I had made was returning to me.
[Unbreakable Faith] grated as it was ground away.
At the time, it had been the best choice.
I had thought I could see the 1863rd round's ending, then return to the third.
So I had tried to find a story where everyone could be happy.
But
If the 1863rd-round Yoo Joonghyuk hadn't helped me then.
If the Han Sooyoung of the 1863rd round had wanted to kill me.
Could I have returned safely to this world?
I had thought I knew the scenarios better than anyone. Had I really only survived through luck?
「Your companions were here.」
One stroke of Yoo Joonghyuk's sword tore my shoulder.
「Your worldline was here.」
The second split my elbow.
「You told people to live in this world.」
The third pierced the base of my wing. It hurt.
But more painful than that pain were the anger and disappointment in his words.
「Incarnation ‘Yoo Joonghyuk’ refuses to regress.」
Yoo Joonghyuk, who had abandoned regression because of me, who had decided to live in the third round, was looking at me.
A being who loved this world more than anyone, and wanted to protect it for that reason, was looking at me.
「But you.」
Some anger, some sense of betrayal, cannot be described in words.
No omniscient reader can read it.
Yoo Hoseong had said,
—A Story may not seem impressive at a glance, but to someone trying to look inside, it reveals a labyrinthine abyss. Even the smallest Story is no different.
What I was seeing now couldn't be all of Yoo Joonghyuk.
I would never know why he was angry.
All of those things could be reasons, and none of them could be.
What was certain was that Yoo Joonghyuk had decided not to be swayed anymore.
By me. By himself.
By those damned constellations who might be watching us even now.
「Answer me, Kim Dokja.」
I staggered under the barrage of sword strikes.
Yoo Joonghyuk probably knew.
That even now, I was reading him.
Knowing I was reading him, he kept thinking without pause.
「Answer.」
Just as I had watched him beyond this wall, he, too, was endlessly writing something from the other side.
Hoping that someday, someone would surely look at that wall.
But I couldn't answer him.
Because if I answered now
[The ‘Fourth Wall’ thickens.]
You would become a character.
[The ‘Fourth Wall’ thickens further.]
Because you must not become a character.
Rumble!
Yoo Joonghyuk, glaring at me with his familiar blazing eyes.
Yoo Joonghyuk existed there.
He was breaking me to prove that he wasn't a character.
「I see.」
His words appeared on the wall.
「That is your choice.」
[The ‘Fourth Wall’ thickens further.]
「There were no companions in this round, either.」
If I gave any answer at all, Yoo Joonghyuk might forgive me.
A miracle might happen, and he might understand me.
But even then, Han Sooyoung wouldn't return.
The wounds we had inflicted on each other wouldn't disappear.
We could no longer be companions.
Both Yoo Joonghyuk and I knew that well.
[The ‘Fourth Wall’ thickens further.]
That was why we charged toward each other, swords in hand.
[The ‘Fourth Wall’ thickens further.]
Full force met full force with a deafening roar. Pale dust billowed up, and neither of us could withstand the impact. We sprawled on the ground.
I was the first to rise.
Staggering toward the battered Yoo Joonghyuk, I pointed my sword at him.
Without resisting, he looked at me and said,
“······I've stayed in this round too long. Finish it.”
Yoo Joonghyuk had killed Han Sooyoung.
We had already crossed the line beyond which there was no turning back.
The tip of [Unbreakable Faith] trembled.
As I raised my sword, the 1863rd-round Han Sooyoung's words came to mind.
―If my novel is a plagiarized copy of Ways of Survival, what are you a plagiarized copy of?
The answer stood before me.
「Kim Dokja learned how to live from this man.」
This man had been my father.
My older brother.
My longtime friend.
[The ‘Fourth Wall’ grows thicker.]
For a long time, I had watched him beyond this thick wall.
He had saved me so many times.
I had survived by watching his story.
[Unbreakable Faith] slowly fell to the ground.
I could neither kill him nor beg forgiveness.
I had never learned to be that cowardly.
What I had learned was to pay the price for what I had done.
Yoo Joonghyuk looked up at me.
And I, too, looked at him.
「I am here.」
I know.
「And still, you only read.」
Because this is our way.
You act, and I read you.
「If you won't do it, I will.」
Slowly rising, Yoo Joonghyuk gripped his sword.
I hear a story coming to an end.
The ‘Mass Production Maker’ had said that some Stories ended without ever approaching their ■■.
But if this was the end of every story.
If I was going to die here anyway, couldn't I at least say one thing too?
“······Yoo Joonghyuk.”
At my words, he stopped.
“As you know, I'm not a prophet. In fact, I'm very far from anything like that.”
Since the day we first fought on Dongho Bridge, I had never properly introduced myself.
To Yoo Joonghyuk, I had been a prophet, an unknown bastard.
“I'm not the Demon King of Salvation, either.”
[The Story, ‘Demon King of Salvation’, stops its story.]
“Nor the King of a Kingless World.”
[The Story, ‘King of a Kingless World’, stops its story.]
One by one, the Stories stopped speaking.
Everything except my story fell silent.
“My name is Kim Dokja.”
The wings that had sprouted from my back disappeared, and my bulging muscles shrank.
“Twenty-eight······ No, I was twenty-eight, and worked at a game company. My hobby was reading webnovels······.”
As though meeting someone for the first time, I continued.
“Boring, isn't it? This is just who I am. ······Yoo Joonghyuk, who are you?”
To me, Yoo Joonghyuk had been someone I had known for a very long time.
More precisely, someone I had been reading, all by myself.
So I had never once heard his story.
Yoo Joonghyuk opened his mouth.
“I am Yoo Joonghyuk.”
His slowly moving blade cut me.
“Yoo Joonghyuk, who was a regressor.”
The moment Han Sooyoung opened her eyes, she vomited blood.
Only after pitch-black blood covered the ground did Han Sooyoung manage to regain her senses. She was deep in a forest. Not on the battlefield where she'd been fighting Yoo Joonghyuk moments earlier.
“I really nearly fucking died. Yoo Joonghyuk, you son of a bitch······.”
If she hadn't transferred her memories at the last moment to a dummy avatar stationed nearby, she really would have died.
[You have exhausted today's allotted ‘Memory Transfer’ power.]
[This avatar will now become your main body.]
It was all as predicted.
[The Story, ‘Predictive Plagiarism’, hesitantly continues its story.]
The Story, 「Predictive Plagiarism」.
A Story she had gained after that mysterious dream.
Through 「Predictive Plagiarism」, Han Sooyoung had clearly seen several scenes.
Predicted futures that changed according to her choices.
Kim Dokja's death, or Yoo Joonghyuk's death.
The single future she could reach by avoiding those terrible choices.
[As a penalty for ‘Memory Transfer’, your physical abilities are greatly weakened.]
“Neither of you had better be dead.”
Grumbling, Han Sooyoung read the surrounding waves of energy. She had to work out which direction they were in, and fast.
Before long, she sensed two powerful sources of Status.
She ran that way.
This was the ‘only proper future’ among those she had read.
Kim Dokja wouldn't die, and the two would have their first proper conversation.
That was what her [Predictive Plagiarism] had predicted, and why she hadn't dodged Yoo Joonghyuk's sword at the last moment.
So Kim Dokja would surely be alive.
Then she heard the crash of sword blows in the distance.
······Were they still fighting?
These bastards. She'd even died so they would talk······.
Apparently, she would have to give them a piece of her mind.
And when she pushed through the undergrowth, the sight before her horrified her.
Booom! Booom!
Yoo Joonghyuk was hacking at Kim Dokja, who lay on the ground.
“Hey! You crazy bastard!”
‘······Is it not working?’
Yoo Joonghyuk looked down at the fallen Kim Dokja.
A thin cut from his [Black Heavenly Demon Sword] marked the unconscious man's chest.
‘I could have sworn I saw it.’
Yoo Joonghyuk concentrated once more, sword in hand.
The next moment, he noticed the dark energy flowing from Kim Dokja's body.
It was a wall. The source of the strange feeling he'd had whenever he saw Kim Dokja.
‘I can see it.’
A pitch-black wall made of countless texts.
Raising his sword upright, he struck the wall again.
As the transcendent's Story pounded it, the wall shook uneasily.
[The ‘Fourth Wall’ glares at you.]
Whether it glared or not, Yoo Joonghyuk struck it.
‘Perhaps beyond this wall.’
If it wouldn't open, until it opened. If it wouldn't break, until it broke. On and on.
Then, the next moment,
“You lunatic! Have you lost it?”
With a shrill voice came a heavy blow to the back of his head. Blood streamed down, obscuring his vision.
His vision tinged red, he saw Han Sooyoung looking down at Kim Dokja.
“Hey! Kim Dokja! Wake up! Wake······ What? You're not dead?”
Yoo Joonghyuk staggered, frowning.
“Han Sooyoung, do you really want to die?”
“You already killed me once, bastard.”
“I knew you wouldn't die.”
“Don't lie. My acting was perfect.”
Growling, Han Sooyoung pointed at her incarnation body (which had been her true body until moments ago), still lying off to one side.
The incarnation body was losing its strength and crumbling, but there were clear traces of bleeding. Blood an [Avatar] shouldn't shed.
Yoo Joonghyuk said,
“Once an [Avatar] holds at least a certain amount of memory, it bleeds like a true body.”
“Oh? And how did you know that?”
“I read it in the record you wrote. Your 1863rd-round self, to be precise.”
“That round's me really wrote down everything. Damn it.”
She had many questions, but chose not to ask.
Instead, she poked the unconscious Kim Dokja's cheek and said,
“Still, looks like this bastard was completely fooled.”
“So it seems.”
“How was he?”
“He came at me like a madman.”
Laughing softly, Han Sooyoung pinched Kim Dokja's cheek as though proud of him.
“What's wrong with his chest?”
“Punishment for making me eat dirt.”
“Something happened.”
Han Sooyoung quietly looked down at Kim Dokja's cheek as she stretched it.
In truth, Kim Dokja was alive, but hardly any part of his body was uninjured. They'd fought hard enough to sweep away the entire surrounding forest; it would have been strange if he'd been unhurt.
All that destruction. Han Sooyoung understood that this was evidence of the conversation Kim Dokja and Yoo Joonghyuk had shared.
“So, did you hear the answer you wanted?”
After a brief pause, Yoo Joonghyuk answered.
“Some of it.”
Han Sooyoung couldn't fully read the depths of feeling in ‘some of it’. That belonged entirely to Kim Dokja and Yoo Joonghyuk. She felt disappointed, and a little lonely.
“You'll come back to <Kim Dokja’s Company>, right?”
Yoo Joonghyuk thought for another moment, then turned as though he had said all he needed to.
Han Sooyoung frowned.
“Hey. Answer properly! After I went to all that trouble to help!”
“The ‘Great War of Saints and Demons’ is almost here.”
He kept walking.
One step, two. Just as Han Sooyoung was about to shout again.
Bzzzzzt!
Amid the sparks, a voice came from Kim Dokja's body.
「(Yoo Joonghyuk-ssi, this isn't the time to worry about some scenario.)」
Startled, Yoo Joonghyuk drew his sword.
The virtual wall surrounding Kim Dokja was moving.
Beyond it, someone was speaking.
「(Do you think you can just do all the talking and then walk away?)」
No, more precisely, it wasn't the wall—
「(You should experience it, too. What it feels like to be a ‘reader’.)」
Bzzzzzt!

A small hole opened in one side of the wall, which hadn't broken however hard he'd struck it, and someone's hand shot out. Easily grabbing Yoo Joonghyuk by the hair, it slammed his head into the wall.
When I came to, I was lying in pitch-black darkness.
What had happened?
Had I died?

With Yoo Sangah in the library, I'd already considered that she might discover memories like these.

All my memories.

All the piled-up books were my stories.
Kim Dokja at fifteen. Kim Dokja at eighteen. Kim Dokja at twenty-three. Kim Dokja at twenty-eight······.

Kim Dokja, who had no father.
Kim Dokja, who had no friends.
Kim Dokja, who had lost his mother.
A life in which something was always missing or being lost.
「A being that is alone does not exist. Kim Dokja was always alone. Thus he was dokja (獨子), a solitary child, and Kim Dokja did not exist.」
A painfully valid sentence.

A life like a long book report on a single book. That was my life.

······Had Yoo Sangah-ssi read this, too?

······Would I still be alive?
Could I have kept living?
「(Would we still be working at the same company?)」
‘My contract wasn't renewed······ so I suppose I'd have been looking for another company.’

I wouldn't have died so easily. Sometimes I would have wanted to die, and on many nights I would have fallen asleep rereading ‘Ways of Survival’······ but I wouldn't have died so easily. Somehow, I would have kept living.
‘In that world, I wouldn't have become close to you either, Yoo Sangah-ssi. I'd have changed companies, and we'd have had no reason to keep in touch.’

Just as ‘Ways of Survival’ had once been to me.

Because they were characters in a novel. They were······.
‘······That would be wonderful.’
「(Oh, Joonghyuk-ssi too. His personality's awful, but he's a good cook, so it'd be nice to become friends.)」
Something suddenly welled up inside me.

With so many worldlines, perhaps just one.

‘Perhaps it does.’
「(Dokja-ssi.)」
‘Yes.’

Taking advantage of the weakened [Fourth Wall], this island's owner was calling her.
······The King of Reincarnators.

One of the reasons we came to Reincarnation Island.

February 15.
